data.body: e27c Phase 4a contract cards frozen. Canonical-dispatch card — authority: ticket mappings and bridge pass-through decisions; preconditions: invoke the real top-level main with bridge fsck/check-access/setup and representative arguments; path: main -> bridge_cli -> existing bridge_fsck.main/_bridge_probe/jira_onboard; tier: in-process public CLI for dependency injection because one tier lower would miss routing; postcondition: exact argv reaches the existing implementation and its exit/stdout/stderr propagate. Compatibility-parity card — authority: additive migration contract; preconditions: canonical and old spellings invoked against the same faked irreversible Jira boundary or real temporary tracker; tier: public CLI plus subprocess where parsing/streams/help matter; postcondition: success/failure/options/output/exit parity, canonical setup usage names its entrypoint, legacy usage remains, fsck has no check-access flag. Stale-vocabulary card — authority: enumerated consumer inventory; preconditions: tracked repository tree; tier: contract grep because source/document vocabulary is itself the contract; postcondition: no uncategorized live old spelling outside compatibility registrations, parity/migration notes, changelog/archive/experiments/ADR history. Negative controls: preview/sync/status/pause/resume and public library/MCP bridge_fsck remain unchanged. Surface census: CLI=in scope through main and subprocess; automated callers=in scope through canary/generator/workflow contract tests and stale guard; library facade=out of rename scope but existing boundary coverage retained; MCP/API=out of rename scope and existing schema coverage retained; dual direction=in scope as old/new aliases route the same core. Contention exempt: this adds no composed lock, retry, or cache; all operations ride existing seams. Gate: make test (all nodes collected/executed, no skip/xfail).
